message.content: Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS + game-server hosting business. Build Phase 1 of a new flagship product: **NxLabs**, a standalone public mod/plugin/texture-pack/shader catalog and installer. ## Critical context from a completed internal survey — read this carefully, it changes the shape of the work A real mod system ALREADY EXISTS in production and must be extended, not rebuilt: - `prisma/schema.prisma`: `model GameMod` (~line 2878, 124 rows seeded) and `model ServerMod` (~line 2936, per-server install state). - `lib/actions-mods.ts` (261 lines): `installMod`/`uninstallMod` etc. — writes a desired-state `ServerMod` row and enqueues a `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job; state-driven, not command-driven. - `worker/game-mods.ts` (372 lines): the real installer. Resolves a direct download URL from Modrinth/SpigotMC(Spiget)/uMod/Thunderstore APIs (`resolveUrl`), then SSHes into the customer's VM and has the VM itself curl the file into the right mod directory. `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = {minecraft, rust, valheim}` in `lib/mod-install-support.ts` — currently only these 3 families are wired end-to-end, even though 124 mods across more families are seeded. - `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx` — the EXISTING per-server "Mods & Plugins" tab inside an individual server's panel (`GamePanelShell.tsx`). This is scoped to one server/one game family and stays as-is — it's the "install from within my server's panel" experience, not what you're building. - `app/(marketing)/game-servers/mods/page.tsx` — an existing marketing page, likely thin, worth checking before you add a new one. - **Confirmed gap**: `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` is referenced (in `schema.prisma` comments, `actions-mods.ts`, `ModsPanel.tsx`) as the thing that populates `verifiedAt`, `downloads`, `fileBytes`, `upstreamOk`, and critically **`iconUrl`** — but this script does not exist anywhere in the repo. Every one of those fields is null/zero/false for all 124 seeded mods today. This is why there are no mod images — not a scraping problem, a missing-script problem. - Dead code to delete: `components/customer/gamepanel/ModStore.tsx` (521 lines, unused, not imported anywhere) — fabricates fake star ratings, install counts, and reviews with invented authors from a slug hash. Delete it before anyone mistakes it for a real component to build on. - Real API keys already configured and tested working this session: `MODRINTH_API_KEY` in `/opt/nxeon/.env` (Modrinth). A CurseForge key was supplied but is currently rejected — treat as unavailable for now, don't block on it. - Storage: no S3/object storage exists in this codebase today. For now, Phase 1 does NOT need to solve creator-upload file storage (defer that) — Phase 1 is about the INDEXED (Modrinth/Thunderstore-sourced) catalog, which never stores files on Nxeon's own infrastructure at all (the installer has customer VMs curl directly from the source, and public downloads should link to the real, authoritative source URL too — legitimate, no hosting/storage problem, matches the licensing approach already agreed this session). - Two real, separate config gaps confirmed by the survey that WILL break this if not fixed: (1) `next.config.ts` has NO `images.remotePatterns`/`domains` configured at all — `next/image` with remote Modrinth/Thunderstore icon URLs will throw. Either add the correct `remotePatterns` for Modrinth's CDN (`cdn.modrinth.com`) and Thunderstore's, or use plain `` tags (CSP already permits `https:` sources) — your call, but confirm one of these actually works in a real browser. (2) No sitemap index exists; you're adding at most ~100-200 pages in this phase (see scope below) which is nowhere near the ~10-25k threshold the survey flagged as needing `generateSitemaps()`, so just add your new slugs to the existing single `app/sitemap.ts` the same way `LANDING_SLUGS` etc. already work — do not build a sitemap index in this phase. ## What "NxLabs" actually is (the owner's own words, this is a hard requirement, not optional) - **A genuinely standalone, public product** — NOT nested inside an individual server's panel. Anyone can browse and download mods/plugins/texture packs/shaders, **even with no Nxeon account and no server at all**. This means real public pages with real download links that work for anonymous visitors. - **A dedicated top-level sidebar entry in the customer portal** — its own page/section, not a tab buried inside `GamePanelShell`. A logged-in customer who has a matching server gets an "Add to my server" action from within this catalog; someone without a matching server (or not logged in) just gets the download link. - **Public marketing/SEO pages** — individual mod pages, discoverable via search, matching the "riddled with SEO" instruction from earlier in this session. Reuse the proven `[slug]`-catch-all + `generateStaticParams` + `sitemap.ts` pattern already used for the location/game-hosting pages (`app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` as the most recent example of this pattern) — do NOT hand-write per-mod page files; there could eventually be thousands. - Real images are mandatory (this is why the verify script matters so much), recommended server resources per mod, and supported game versions — these were explicit requirements from the owner. ## Concrete Phase 1 scope (do not try to build everything — this is intentionally the first slice) 1. **Write `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`.** For every seeded `GameMod` row sourced from Modrinth (check `source` field), call the real Modrinth API (`MODRINTH_API_KEY` in `.env`) to fetch and store: `iconUrl` (gallery/icon image), `downloads`, real license info if the schema has a field for it (check; add one via migration if genuinely needed, following this codebase's `String`-with-comment enum convention, not a Prisma enum), `verifiedAt` (now), `upstreamOk` (true if the API call succeeded and the project still exists, false + a reason if 404/removed). For Thunderstore/SpigotMC/uMod-sourced mods, do the equivalent against each of those APIs if reasonably quick to add; if a source's API integration would be substantial new work, it's fine to leave those `upstreamOk: false, verifiedAt: null` for this phase and note it clearly in your report — don't let scope creep here block shipping the Modrinth-sourced majority. Make this idempotent and re-runnable (an admin should be able to re-run it periodically to catch dead links / new downloads counts — this is also the "mark as no longer supported" mechanism the owner asked about: `upstreamOk: false` after a re-verify IS that marker, wire `GameMod.active`/`upstreamOk` display to reflect "no longer supported" in the UI you build). 2. **Public catalog browse + individual mod pages**, backed by real DB data (verified in step 1), under the proven `[slug]` marketing pattern: - A browse/index page (e.g. `/mods` or `/nxlabs` — pick one consistent root, check for naming collisions with the existing `/game-servers/mods` page and either replace/redirect it or clearly differentiate) listing real mods with real icons, filterable by game family. - Individual mod detail pages (e.g. `/mods//` given `GameMod`'s `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` isn't globally unique) with: real image, description, supported game version(s) (from the mod's real version data), a real download link (pointing at the authoritative source, e.g. Modrinth's own CDN file URL — do not proxy/mirror the actual file through Nxeon's infrastructure in this phase), and recommended server resources (derive sensibly from the mod's category/size — even a simple heuristic like "works on any plan ≥ X GB RAM" tied to the relevant `GamePlan` tiers is fine for Phase 1; don't over-engineer this). - SEO: real `generateMetadata`, and reuse `ProductJsonLd`/`FaqJsonLd` structured-data helpers from `components/marketing/StructuredData.tsx` where they genuinely fit (do NOT add `AggregateRating` — the survey confirmed no real review data exists yet; other pages in this codebase deliberately omit it for exactly this reason, follow that same discipline). - Add the new slugs into `app/sitemap.ts` the same way existing slug arrays are wired in. 3. **New top-level portal page** (not inside `GamePanelShell`): a dedicated "NxLabs" entry in `lib/nx/nav.ts` (check `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`'s separate legacy nav array + `FEATURE_HREF` map too — the survey found these can silently drift out of sync, make sure a new item respects any feature-flag gating the same way existing items do) linking to a new `/dashboard/nxlabs` (or similar) page: the same catalog, but for a LOGGED-IN customer, showing "Add to my server" wherever they have a real server whose `gameFamily` matches the mod (reuse the existing `installMod` action from `lib/actions-mods.ts` — do not fork a second install code path; if they have multiple matching servers, let them pick which one, a simple picker is fine). If they have no matching server, just show the same public download link. 4. **Fix the two config gaps** (images remotePatterns or `` decision; nothing else needed for sitemap at this scale). 5. **Delete `components/customer/gamepanel/ModStore.tsx`** (confirmed dead/unused). 6. **Admin "mark no longer supported" control.** Per the owner's explicit ask: add a simple admin surface (or extend an existing one if `GameMod` already has any admin page — check) to view `GameMod` rows and toggle `active`/see `upstreamOk`, following the established action pattern (`requireAdmin()` first, `FormState` shape, `revalidatePath`, real `recordAudit` from `lib/audit.ts` — NOT a local reimplementation) from `lib/actions-nodes.ts`/`components/admin/NodeForms.tsx` as the reference. This can be a straightforward list+toggle, doesn't need to be elaborate in Phase 1. ## Explicitly OUT of scope for this phase (do not build) Creator upload program, object storage, reviews/ratings, Bedrock/Factorio family expansion, post-install auto-restart, CurseForge integration, any actual file scraping or mirroring of copyrighted binaries. ## Process - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Real browser verification (Playwright): the public browse page, at least 2 individual mod pages with real images actually rendering (not broken image icons), and the logged-in portal NxLabs page showing an "Add to my server" action for an account with a real matching server. Check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule — don't build in /opt/nxeon directly. - Credential hygiene: DB reads via `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run with `npx tsx`. Never print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` string. - Deploy: commit → push → `deploy-staging.sh` → verify 200 → `promote-production.sh` → verify 200 and a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (record `cat /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID` first). Other agents may be concurrently deploying unrelated work — if a deploy collides, retry once after confirming staging is healthy, never revert someone else's work. Report back: how many `GameMod` rows actually got real verified data (icons/downloads) after running the verify script, the real public URLs for the browse page and 2+ mod detail pages, confirmation images render in a real browser, confirmation the portal NxLabs page and "Add to my server" work end-to-end against a real account, confirmation of the admin toggle, and the production deploy confirmation with fresh BUILD_ID.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

EssentialsX is the essential plugin suite for Spigot and Paper servers, including over 130 commands and countless features for servers of any scale!

EssentialsX is a modern continuation of the original Essentials suite for Bukkit, with support for the latest Minecraft versions.  
EssentialsX also includes several performance enhancements and fixes on top of the original Essentials, as well as plenty of new useful features for servers.
You can view major differences and learn how to set EssentialsX up over at the [EssentialsX website](https://essentialsx.net/).

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

input.new_string: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. --- ## NxLabs — standalone public mod/plugin catalog, Phase 1 (2026-09-19) A real mod system already existed (`GameMod`/`ServerMod`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts`, the per-server `ModsPanel.tsx` tab) but was reachable only from inside one server's own panel, and every verified-fact column on `GameMod` (icon, downloads, license, versions, upstream health) had sat empty since seeding — nothing ever populated them. NxLabs is the standalone product layer on top: a public, no-account-required catalog + a logged-in portal page, both reading the same now-real data. **`scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` (new).** Idempotent, re-runnable verification pass against each mod's real upstream API. Covers `modrinth` (Modrinth API v2, using `MODRINTH_API_KEY`), `spigotmc` (the public Spiget API), and `thunderstore` (Thunderstore's experimental package API) — the same three sources `worker/game-mods.ts` already knows how to install from. Writes `iconUrl`, `downloads`, `license` (new `GameMod` column, string not enum — see schema comment), `gameVersions`, `loaders`, `fileBytes`, `dependencyCount`, `serverSide`, `impact`/`impactNote` (heuristic from real file size), `verifiedAt`, and `upstreamOk` + new `upstreamNote` (why, when false). First run: 58 of 124 seeded mods verified (53 real + 5 correctly flagged no-longer-supported — all 5 genuinely `is_deprecated` on Thunderstore); `umod`, `github`, `nexus`, `codefling` (66 rows) intentionally left unverified — none has a lightweight give-me-this-exact-project-by-id API the way the three above do, and the UI already renders "unverified" honestly rather than guessing. Re-running is the "mark no longer supported" mechanism: a project that 404s on a later pass flips `upstreamOk` to false automatically. Found and fixed live during the first run: Spiget's `existenceStatus` field is NOT a reliable "removed" signal — it returned the integer `1` for indisputably-live resources with millions of downloads (Vault, CMI, ProtocolLib). The script no longer reads it at all; only a real HTTP 404 from the API marks a SpigotMC resource gone. **Public catalog** — `app/(marketing)/mods` (browse, filterable by game family via `?family=`) and `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]` (detail: real icon, description, license, supported versions, a recommended-plan heuristic tied to real active `GamePlan` rows, and a real download link resolved live from the source — Modrinth's own CDN file URL, Spiget's download redirect, or Thunderstore's — never a Nxeon-hosted mirror). Both filtered to `active && upstreamOk` only. `lib/mods-catalog.ts` is the shared read layer (also feeds the dashboard page and `app/sitemap.ts`). No `AggregateRating`/review data — none of it is real. Distinct from the pre-existing `/game-servers/mods` page, which stays as the "our hosting includes a Mod Store" marketing pitch; the two now cross-link. **Portal page** — `app/dashboard/nxlabs` (new top-level nav entry, `lib/nx/nav.ts`, and kept in sync in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`'s legacy nav array): the same catalog, with a real matching-server "Add to my server" control (`components/mods/QuickAddButton.tsx`) that calls the EXISTING `installMod()` action — no second install path. `components/mods/AddToServerWidget.tsx` is the equivalent for the public detail page, which has to handle "not logged in" as a normal state (`getEligibleServersForMod()`, new, soft on auth). **Admin** — `/admin/game-mods` (new "Mods" tab under the Catalog nav section, `requireArea("billing")`): view every `GameMod` row with its real verified facts, toggle `active`, and toggle `upstreamOk` by hand with a note (`lib/actions-admin-gamemods.ts`, uses the shared `recordAudit()`, not an ad hoc write). **Config gaps closed.** `next.config.ts` had no `images.remotePatterns` — NxLabs icons come from whichever source verified them (Modrinth's CDN today, more as the verify script grows), so plain `` tags are used instead of `next/image` (the CSP's `img-src https:` already permits it; confirmed rendering in a real browser) rather than maintaining a growing per-CDN allowlist. `app/sitemap.ts` gained `/mods` + one entry per active/verified mod, via `listCatalogSlugs()` — same pattern as the existing slug arrays, no sitemap index needed at this scale (~124 mods, nowhere near the ~10-25k threshold). **Removed:** `components/customer/gamepanel/ModStore.tsx` (521 lines, dead — not imported anywhere, fabricated star ratings/install counts/reviews from a slug hash). **Out of scope, deliberately:** creator uploads, object storage, reviews/ratings, CurseForge, umod/github/ nexus/codefling verification, post-install auto-restart, mirroring any file through Nxeon's own infra. **Entry points.** `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`; `lib/mods-catalog.ts`; `lib/actions-mods.ts` (`getEligibleServersForMod`); `lib/actions-admin-gamemods.ts`; `components/mods/{ModCard, AddToServerWidget,QuickAddButton}.tsx`; `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`; `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`; `app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx`; `app/admin/game-mods/page.tsx`; `components/admin/GameModControls.tsx`; `lib/nx/nav.ts`; `lib/admin-groups.ts`; `prisma/schema.prisma` (`GameMod.license`, `GameMod.upstreamNote`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. --- *Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (server migration).*

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy

content.text: This builds directly in `/opt/nxeon`. Given the build-isolation memory warning, let's check further — the script itself is the sanctioned promote path, so it's expected to build there.

content.content:
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"

input.prompt:
On the Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), the Content-Security-Policy in next.config.ts's `script-src` directive does not include `https://connect.facebook.net` or `https://googleads.g.doubleclick.net` (or the wider Google Ads/Analytics conversion domains it calls out to). Confirmed live via Playwright against https://nxeon.cloud/mods and https://nxeon.cloud/mods/minecraft/essentialsx just now: the browser console shows repeated CSP violations blocking `https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js` and `https://googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/viewthroughconversion/...` script loads, on ordinary page views (not something specific to the mods pages — this is a shared root-level CSP header applied site-wide via next.config.ts's headers()).

Given this repo's history has real Meta Pixel + Google Ads conversion tracking work (server-side CAPI, PageView SPA re-fire, offline conversion upload), a CSP gap that silently blocks the pixel/conversion scripts in every real visitor's browser would mean ad platforms are undercounting or missing conversions entirely, with no visible error to anyone except someone reading the browser console.

Please:
1. Confirm which script/host each blocked call actually needs (check components/marketing/PurchaseTracker.tsx, SignupTracker.tsx, and wherever the Meta Pixel snippet and Google Ads gtag/conversion snippet are loaded from, to get the precise, minimal set of hosts — don't just allowlist broadly).
2. Add exactly those hosts to next.config.ts's `script-src` (and `connect-src`/`img-src` if the pixel also fires background beacons/images that CSP would separately block — check for `www.facebook.com/tr` pixel-image fallback too).
3. Verify live in a real browser (Playwright) on a few real pages that no CSP violations remain in the console for these trackers, and that nothing else broke.
4. Deploy through the normal pipeline (staging verify -> promote-production), and update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md per this repo's "every change updates the docs" rule.

content.text:
## Summary

I built and shipped **NxLabs Phase 1** — a standalone public mod/plugin catalog — on top of the existing `GameMod`/`ServerMod` system, per the spec. Everything is live in production.

**Verify script (`scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`, new):** Real Modrinth + SpigotMC(Spiget) + Thunderstore API verification, idempotent/re-runnable. Final result on production: **58 of 124 seeded mods verified** — **53 with real data** (icons, downloads, license, versions, file size) and **5 correctly flagged `upstreamOk:false`** (genuinely deprecated on Thunderstore, with a human-readable `upstreamNote`). **52 mods have real icons.** uMod/GitHub/Nexus/Codefling (66 rows) intentionally left unverified per the agreed scope — no lightweight per-project API for those sources. Found and fixed a real bug mid-run: Spiget's `existenceStatus` field returned integer `1` for indisputably-live resources (Vault, CMI, ProtocolLib) — it's not a "removed" signal, so the script no longer reads it, relying only on real HTTP 404s.

**Live public URLs (production):**
- Browse: https://nxeon.cloud/mods (filterable by family)
- Detail: https://nxeon.cloud/mods/minecraft/essentialsx, https://nxeon.cloud/mods/minecraft/luckperms — confirmed via Playwright that real icons render (double-checked the EssentialsX icon against Modrinth's own CDN directly — it's genuinely a red flask logo, not a bug), with real license/downloads/versions/recommended-plan and a real download link resolved live from the source.

**Portal + "Add to my server":** New `/dashboard/nxlabs` (nav entry added to `lib/nx/nav.ts`, kept in sync in the legacy array). End-to-end verified on **staging** with a real throwaway test account + real Minecraft server: clicking "Add to my server" created a real `ServerMod` row and `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job that the worker processed to `INSTALLED`/`DONE` — using the existing `installMod()` action, no forked path. Same flow gated correctly (login prompt) for anonymous visitors on the public detail page.

**Admin (`/admin/game-mods`):** Deployed, correctly gated (307/404 as appropriate on both hosts), and renders real data (124 mods, verified/unverified/unsupported badges) — confirmed via an authenticated staging session. The interactive toggle-click itself was **inconclusive** due to a pre-existing, unrelated infra bug (staging's admin subdomain nginx vhost proxies to node-2 instead of this box — flagged as `task_7f5f00b5`); the action code is a verbatim mirror of the already-proven `adminToggleGamePlan` pattern using the shared `recordAudit()`.

**Deploy:** Commit `2fe13e0632` pushed to `main`. Staging verified (200, real data after seeding+verifying its DB too). Production promoted — first attempt hit a build-worker OOM from concurrent box load (retried per the "collision" instructions, second attempt succeeded). **Fresh BUILD_ID: `BJ_iwJGmMl-qks-R2HbVQ`** (was `z9srsQqJaregrBEwT3vre`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout.

**Two things flagged for separate follow-up (not fixed by me, out of scope):** the staging-admin nginx misroute above, and a pre-existing sitewide CSP gap blocking Meta Pixel/Google Ads scripts on every page (`task_e5939d6d`) — found incidentally while browser-testing, unrelated to NxLabs.

**Note:** while I was working, another agent picked up this exact commit and is actively extending it further (uncommitted, staged changes for ratings/store-browser UI visible in `git status`) — I left that untouched (didn't commit, didn't discard) since it's someone else's in-flight work; I double-checked production is unaffected by it.

**Key files:** `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `lib/actions-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-gamemods.ts`, `app/(marketing)/mods/{page.tsx,[family]/[slug]/page.tsx}`, `app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx`, `app/admin/game-mods/page.tsx`, `components/mods/*`, `prisma/schema.prisma` (added `license`, `upstreamNote`), `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` and `ROADMAP.md` updated per repo convention.
